# Injury Risk: Injured, Recovering and Chronic Cases

**Summary.** Mark down chronic cases (repeated surgeries or problems in the same lower-body spot, or an ongoing mystery illness) below their per-game value, even after a healthy year. Do not overreact to one-off injuries, which are often underpriced. Our 4 IL slots only take players tagged out (O), not questionable (Q), so plan any stash around the Yahoo status on draft day, 2026-10-18.

## Chronic or one-off: the pricing rule

Sort every injured player into one of two groups before the auction. Chronic means repeated injuries or surgeries to the same lower-body part, above all knees, or an ongoing mystery illness. One-off means a single injury, or a hand, finger, shoulder or oblique problem. Those upper-body injuries matter little. Concussions matter a little. ([08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=873))

Chronic cases miss more time in the future. Bid on them below their per-game value. A healthy season does not remove a degenerative risk, so do not pay last year's price because he stayed healthy. In practice, take your per-game price for a chronic case and stop bidding clearly below it. ([06-30](https://youtu.be/JMSLg6yz-M0?t=380), [06-30](https://youtu.be/JMSLg6yz-M0?t=547), [08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=873))

One-off cases are different. Avoid players who start the season injured, but our season is 25 weeks long. A short absence costs a few games out of about 25 weeks, so a short-term injury should take only a few dollars off a fair bid. ([09-27](https://youtu.be/CRLSsoGhb2w?t=561))

## Coming back from injury and minutes limits

A player returning from injury usually has a minutes limit and misses back-to-backs. While he ramps up, all of his numbers drop, not just his games played. In 9-cat that hurts every counting category at once. Take this ramp-up cost into account on top of any missed games. ([10-04](https://youtu.be/tnzmsYUA4yQ?t=1700), [07-20](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=386))

The experts disagree on how hard to discount returning players. One note says drafters are too scared of players coming back from an injury that cost them last season, and that you can be more confident than their ADP suggests. Other notes stress the hidden cost of minutes limits and rested back-to-backs during the ramp-up. A workable middle path: if the injury was one-off, trust the cheap price and buy. If it was the same lower-body spot again, keep the chronic discount. ([09-21](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=1258), [10-04](https://youtu.be/tnzmsYUA4yQ?t=1700), [07-20](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=386), [06-30](https://youtu.be/JMSLg6yz-M0?t=547))

Back-to-back counts matter mostly for injury-prone players. For chronic cases and load-managed players, check how many back-to-backs their team has in weeks 19 to 21, the playoff weeks ending 2027-03-28. For healthy players, do not let back-to-back counts drive your bid. ([09-29](https://youtu.be/sf6Ga9k-r-Q?t=1686))

## Using our 4 IL slots

Yahoo removed IL+. A player tagged out (O) or injured can go to an IL slot right away. Questionable, doubtful and probable players cannot. So a Q-tagged player takes up one of your 12 active or bench spots until his tag changes. Check each target's Yahoo tag on 2026-10-18, not just the injury news. ([09-21](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=292))

Do not draft or stash a long-term injured player with real auction money. Hold him only while an IL slot would otherwise sit empty, and drop him once you need the spot. An O-tagged player bought for 1 USD with your last pick can go straight to IL, which frees the roster spot for a waiver claim. That is the most a stash should cost you. ([09-14](https://youtu.be/t4n9MAP2_14?t=2182), [09-21](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=292))

During the season, do not drop a player with a short-term injury in a panic. If he is tagged O, move him to IL and use your FAB and the 6 weekly acquisitions to replace his games. ([09-27](https://youtu.be/CRLSsoGhb2w?t=561), [09-21](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=292))

## Do not stack risks

Do not stack several players you have injury worries about. Before every bid on a risky player, count the big risks already on your roster. A practical cap for our 12-man roster is one or two chronic cases among your top spenders. Fill the rest with players who have a clean or one-off history. ([08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1769), [09-24](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=1343))

This matters more in H2H than in roto. Two stars missing the same week can cost you most of the nine categories that week. In the playoffs, one bad week ends your season. If you already hold two chronic cases, let the next one go to another manager, even at a fair price. ([09-24](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=1343), [08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1769), [09-29](https://youtu.be/sf6Ga9k-r-Q?t=1686))
